name: AI Certifications for Veterans
objectives: Given your military job code, identify two or three civilian job titles that match your military job, using My Next Move for Veterans and with no classified details in any prompt
Given at least five real job posts for your target job, identify the certification employers ask for most and confirm its rules on the certification body's website, using a tally of the posts

Given the official exam outline, your weeks and your hours, create a week-by-week study plan with an AI assistant, with a goal each week, a review week and a practice test

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Translating your military job into civilian job titles
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Turn your military job code into two or three civilian job titles.
This lesson builds toward: Given your military job code, you will identify two or three civilian job titles that match your military job, using My Next Move for Veterans and with no classified details in any prompt.
Civilian hiring managers rarely know what an MOS, rating or AFSC means. Your first job is to translate it into the job titles they use, such as "IT support specialist", "logistics coordinator" or "maintenance technician".
My Next Move for Veterans (mynextmove.org/vets), run for the U.S. Department of Labor, lets you type your branch and military job code or title and see civilian careers with similar work.
An AI assistant can help too. Ask it to explain your duties in civilian words, then compare its answer with My Next Move. Do not paste classified details, unit names or anything you were told not to share.
Step by step:
- Open mynextmove.org/vets.
- Under the military section, choose your branch and type your job code or title.
- Write down two or three civilian careers it suggests.
- Ask an AI assistant: "I was an Army 25B (IT specialist). Describe my duties in civilian words for a job post."
- Keep the job titles that appear in both places.
Words to know:
- MOS / rating / AFSC: the codes the services use for military jobs (Army and Marine Corps MOS, Navy and Coast Guard ratings, Air Force AFSC).
- Job title: the name an employer gives a job in a job post.
Official sources:
- My Next Move for Veterans (U.S. Department of Labor)
Try it now: Look up your own military job on mynextmove.org/vets and ask an AI assistant to describe your duties in civilian words. Write down the two civilian job titles that appear in both.
You can now turn your military job code into civilian job titles an employer will recognize.

check.q: What does My Next Move for Veterans do?
options: Shows civilian careers similar to your military job
check.why: You enter your military job and it shows similar civilian careers.

check.q: You ask an AI to describe your duties in civilian words. What do you leave out of the prompt?
options: The number of people you supervised
The kind of equipment you maintained
check.why: General duties are fine, but classified details and unit information never go into a public AI.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Finding the certification employers ask for
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Find the one certification that shows up most in real job posts for your target job.
This lesson builds toward: Given at least five real job posts for your target job, you will identify the certification employers ask for most and confirm its rules on the certification body's website, using a tally of the posts.
A certification is proof from an outside organization that you passed a test on a skill. Employers list the ones they want in their job posts, so job posts are the best guide.
Search a job site for your target job title and your area. Read five to ten posts and tally every certification named. The one that appears most is usually your first target.
Each service runs a Credentialing Opportunities On-Line (COOL) website that links military jobs to related certifications. Ask your education office or search "COOL" with your branch name. Always check the certification body's own website for the current test, rules and price.
AI can help you compare two certifications, but it can be out of date. Use it to explain, not to decide prices or rules.
Step by step:
- Search a job site for your target job title.
- Read five to ten posts and list every certification named.
- Tally them; circle the most common one.
- Check your branch's COOL site for how it links to your military job.
- Open the certification body's own website for the current exam details.
Words to know:
- Certification: proof from an outside organization that you passed a test on a skill.
- Certification body: the organization that writes the test and gives the certification.
- COOL: Credentialing Opportunities On-Line, the services' websites that link military jobs to civilian credentials.
Try it now: Read at least five real job posts for one of your civilian job titles. Make a tally of the certifications they name and circle the most common one.
You can now use real job posts to choose the certification employers want most.

options: Proof from an outside organization that you passed a skill test
check.why: A certification is earned by passing a test set by an outside certification body.

check.q: Three of your five job posts name the same certification. What do you do?
options: Pick a different one that sounds harder
Circle it as your target and check its rules on the certification body's site
Ignore the posts and ask the AI
check.why: The certification named most in real posts is what employers want; its current rules come from the certification body.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Checking what the GI Bill can pay
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Check on va.gov whether VA can repay your certification test fee and how to ask for it.
This lesson builds toward: For your target certification, you will check on va.gov whether VA can repay the test fee and how to ask for it, writing down the limit, the qualifying benefits and the form from the official page.
VA can pay you back for licensing and certification test fees, including registration and administrative fees. When we checked va.gov in October 2026, the limit was no more than $2,000 per test, and VA takes the amount it repays out of your GI Bill entitlement. It does not pay for the certificate itself.
You must already have one of these benefits: the Post-9/11 GI Bill, the Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty or Selected Reserve, or Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance. To ask for the money, send VA Form 22-0803 with the fee receipt and your test results or certificate.
VA also lists other ways to use benefits, such as prep courses, non-college degree programs and the VET TEC 2.0 high-tech training program, which has a limited number of places each year. Rules and amounts change, so open the official page before you spend money.
Step by step:
- Open va.gov and find the licensing and certification test fee page.
- Check you have one of the listed GI Bill benefits.
- Note the current limit and that it uses some of your entitlement.
- Keep your test receipt and your results.
- Submit VA Form 22-0803 as the page explains.
Words to know:
- Entitlement: the amount of GI Bill benefit you have left to use.
- Reimbursement: being paid back for money you already spent.
Official sources:
- VA: Licensing and certification test fees
- VA: How to use your GI Bill benefits
- VA: VET TEC 2.0
Try it now: Open the va.gov test fee page. Write down the current limit, which benefits qualify, and the form number. Then check whether you have one of those benefits.
You can now check on va.gov whether VA can repay a certification test fee and what you need to send.

check.q: What happens to your GI Bill when VA repays a test fee?
options: The amount is taken from your entitlement
check.why: Test fee repayment uses part of your GI Bill entitlement.

check.q: A forum post says VA pays any test fee in full. What do you do?
options: Check the current rules on the official va.gov test fee page
Trust the post because many people liked it
Ask the AI to confirm it
check.why: Benefit rules and limits change, so you confirm them on the official va.gov page.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Building a study plan with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use an AI assistant to turn the official exam outline into a week-by-week study plan.
This lesson builds toward: Given the official exam outline, your weeks and your hours, you will create a week-by-week study plan with an AI assistant, with a goal each week, a review week and a practice test.
Most certification bodies publish an exam outline, sometimes called exam objectives. It lists every topic the test covers. This is your mission brief.
Copy the main topics (not the whole document if it is long) into an AI assistant and give it your situation: how many weeks you have, how many hours a week, and what you already know from the military.
Ask for a plan with a goal for each week, a review week before the test, and a practice test date. Then put the sessions on your calendar like duty times.
Step by step:
- Download the official exam outline from the certification body.
- Tell the AI your weeks, hours per week and what you already know.
- Paste the main topics and ask for a week-by-week plan.
- Ask it to add a review week and a practice test.
- Put each study session on your calendar.
Words to know:
- Exam outline (objectives): the official list of topics a certification test covers.
- Study plan: a schedule saying what you will study and when.
Try it now: Get the exam outline for your target certification. Ask an AI assistant: "I have 8 weeks and 6 hours a week. I already know [what you know]. Make a week-by-week study plan for these topics: [topics]."
You can now turn an official exam outline into a week-by-week study plan with an AI assistant.

options: A practice test from a website
The official list of topics the test covers
A list of past test answers
check.why: The exam outline from the certification body lists exactly what the test covers.

check.q: You have 10 weeks and 5 hours a week. What do you give the AI for your study plan?
options: Your login for the exam site
The exam topics, 10 weeks, 5 hours a week and what you already know
check.why: Topics, time and what you know let the AI build a realistic week-by-week plan.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Practicing with AI the right way
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI to quiz you and explain mistakes, while checking it against official material.
This lesson builds toward: When you practice for the exam, you will use AI to quiz you and explain your mistakes, checking it against official material, using no brain dumps or leaked test questions.
AI is a good study partner. It can quiz you on one topic, explain a wrong answer in simpler words, or give you a real-world example from your military job.
It can also be wrong or out of date. If its answer disagrees with the official study guide or exam outline, trust the official material.
Never use "brain dumps" (copies of real test questions). They break the certification body's rules and can cost you the certification. Practice to understand, not to memorize answers.
Step by step:
- Ask: "Quiz me with 5 questions on [one topic]. Wait for my answer each time."
- When you miss one, ask it to explain in simple words.
- Ask for an example from your military job.
- Check any answer you doubt in the official study guide.
- Track your weak topics and study them again.
Words to know:
- Brain dump: a copy of real test questions shared against the rules; using one can cost you the certification.
- Practice test: a test made for practice that is like the real one but not copied from it.
Try it now: Pick the first topic in your study plan. Ask an AI assistant to quiz you with five questions, one at a time. For every miss, ask for a simple explanation and check it in the official material.
You can now use AI to quiz yourself and explain mistakes, while checking it against official material.

options: Leaked real test questions shared against the rules
A study plan made by AI
check.why: Brain dumps share real test questions, which breaks the rules and can cost you the certification.

check.q: You missed a practice question from the AI. What do you do next?
options: Memorize the AI's answer without checking
Ask the AI to explain it simply and check it in the official guide
check.why: AI explanations help, but the official guide is the final word.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Showing your certification to employers
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Write the résumé line and a short story that show your certification and your service together.
This lesson builds toward: When you earn or are working toward the certification, you will write a résumé line that shows the certification and your service together, with the full name, the certification body and the year or test date.
Once you pass, put the certification where employers look: a "Certifications" section on your résumé with the full name, the certification body and the year, plus your online profile.
Connect it to your service. For example: "Managed network access for 300 users as an Army IT specialist; earned [certification name] in 2026." The certification proves the skill; your service proves you used it under pressure.
Still studying? You can write "[certification name], in progress, test date [month year]". Ask an AI assistant to help with wording, then make sure every word is true.
Step by step:
- Add a Certifications section to your résumé.
- Write the full certification name, the body and the year.
- Add one résumé line that links it to something you did in service.
- If still studying, write "in progress" with your test month.
- Read it out loud and check every word is true.
Words to know:
- Résumé: a one- or two-page summary of your work, training and skills for employers.
Try it now: Final task: make your one-page Certification Plan with your job titles, target certification, the VA page you checked, your AI study plan, and the résumé line you will add when you pass.
You can now plan, fund, study for and show off a certification that fits your military experience.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Civilian job titles No civilian titles, or titles that do not match the military job. The military job and two matching civilian job titles. The titles appear on both My Next Move for Veterans and the AI's description. Target certification The certification was guessed or chosen from an ad. The certification that appears most in at least five real job posts. Shows the tally and the certification body's page checked for current rules. VA payment checked No VA check, or information from a forum or AI only. Whether VA can pay the test fee, with the official va.gov page named. Also notes the form and that repayment uses entitlement. Study plan No plan, or a plan without weeks or topics. A week-by-week plan from the official exam outline with a review week and practice test. The plan fits the learner's real hours and has a set test date. Résumé line No résumé line, or one that claims a certification not yet earned. A true résumé line with the full name, body and year or test date, linked to service. Includes a short story of a result from service that the certification backs up. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: What goes in your résumé's Certifications section?
options: The full name, the certification body and the year
check.why: Employers need the full name, who issued it and when.

check.q: Your test is in March and you have not passed yet. How do you list it?
options: Leave out that you are studying
check.why: Listing it as in progress with a test date is honest and shows your plan.
